test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper provides successive discounts of 2% and 5%, which are equivalent to a single discount of ________
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net discount for two **successive discounts** a% and b% = (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Given **a = 2%** and **b = 5%**.

Equivalent discount = (2 + 5 − (2 × 5) ÷ 100)% = (7 − 10 ÷ 100)%.

Equivalent discount = (7 − 0.1)% = 6.9%.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First discount = 2%, Second discount = 5%.

**Formulas:** Successive Discount = a + b − ab ÷ 100 | Selling Price = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f9593774edd72233ca748f9eb55567007921a34586e241754d111504ee947f08.png] 

⇒ Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100 units.

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 100 − (2% of 100) = 100 − 2 = 98 units.

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 98 − (5% of 98) = 98 − 4.9 = 93.1 units.

⇒ Total discount amount = 100 − 93.1 = 6.9 units.

⇒ **Equivalent single discount** = (6.9 ÷ 100) × 100 = 6.9%.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When a series of discounts are applied one after another on the reducing balance, they are called **successive discounts**. The total effective discount is always less than the simple sum of individual discounts.

Marked Price & Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. The price after deducting the discount is the **Selling Price (SP)**.</p
